https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159730-803392672.png

Diffusion Models' own closing recap, already covered in Diffusion Models, pointed forward here. Autoregressive Models, closing out this module with yet another generative approach, take a genuinely sequential path to generation.
They genuinely generate one piece of data at a time, each new piece conditioned on everything generated so far, an idea explored in full throughout this topic.

This connects back to Diffusion Models' own closing recap, already covered in Diffusion Models. Autoregressive models were genuinely previewed there as the module's own closing approach, briefly described in that earlier topic.

3. One Piece At A Time
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159730-340238852.png
This connects back to the autoregressive generation loop, already covered generally in Sampling. An autoregressive model genuinely generates output one piece at a time, in a fixed order.
Each genuinely new piece is conditioned directly on every piece already generated before it, a genuinely simple, sequential structure explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Chain Rule Factorization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159731-681270028.png

This connects back to generating one piece at a time, already covered in this topic. This genuinely breaks one giant joint probability into a genuine product of many simpler conditional probabilities.
This is the genuinely same chain rule factorization already covered generally in Large Language Models, applied here to the general case of any autoregressive generative model.

https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159731-346738533.png

This connects back to chain rule factorization, already covered in this topic. Transformer decoder architectures, already covered generally in Transformers, are themselves genuinely autoregressive models.

Each genuinely generated token conditions directly on every previously generated token, already covered as causal masking elsewhere in this course, a genuinely concrete, familiar example of this topic's own general idea.

blocks.text: 6. Pixel By Pixel Image Generation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159731-836158291.png
This connects back to one piece at a time, already covered in this topic. The genuinely same idea extends to images, generating one pixel at a time in a fixed scan order.
Each genuinely new pixel conditions on every pixel already generated before it in that scan order, a genuinely direct extension of the sequential idea explored throughout the rest of this topic.
7. Exact Likelihood Advantage
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159731-601679096.png
This connects back to the chain rule factorization, already covered in this topic. Autoregressive models genuinely compute an exact probability for any given piece of data.
This happens unlike GANs, already covered in GANs, which genuinely provide no direct way to score a sample's own probability, a genuinely real advantage explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 8. Sequential Generation Cost
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446159732-343363894.png
This connects back to generating one piece at a time, already covered in this topic. Genuinely producing a long output requires genuinely running the model once for every single piece.

This genuinely makes generation considerably slower than approaches producing an entire sample all at once, a genuinely real cost weighed against the exact likelihood advantage already covered earlier in this topic.
9. Recognizing When Autoregressive Models Are Genuinely The Right Choice
This connects back to genuinely needing exact probability scoring, already covered in this topic. Autoregressive models, already covered in this topic, directly deliver exactly that scoring.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates the chain rule factorization, already covered in this topic, computing a sequence probability step by step.

code.content:
# already covered as conditional probabilities in this topic
conditional_probs = {
    "the": 0.4,               # P("the")
    "the cat": 0.3,            # P("cat" | "the")
    "the cat sat": 0.5,        # P("sat" | "the cat")
    "the cat sat on": 0.6,     # P("on" | "the cat sat")
}

def sequence_probability(conditional_probs):
    # already covered as chain rule factorization in this topic
    joint_probability = 1.0
    for prefix, prob in conditional_probs.items():
        joint_probability *= prob
        print(f"  after '{prefix}': running joint probability = {joint_probability:.5f}")
    return joint_probability

print("Building up the full sequence probability (already covered in this topic), one piece at a time:")
final_probability = sequence_probability(conditional_probs)
print(f"\nFinal sequence probability (already covered as the exact likelihood advantage in this topic): {final_probability:.5f}")

blocks.text: 11. Generative Models: Module Complete

items: Autoregressive models generate one piece of data at a time, conditioned on everything generated so far.
This breaks one joint probability into a product of simpler conditional probabilities, the chain rule.
Transformer decoder architectures are themselves a concrete example of autoregressive models.
The same idea extends to images, generating one pixel at a time in a fixed scan order.
Autoregressive models compute exact probabilities for data, unlike GANs.
Generating a long output requires running the model once per piece, making generation slower.
Autoregressive models suit tasks needing exact probability scoring over raw generation speed.
